title: Getting Started with Templates
description: Learn how to set up and customize your Astro template with themes, internationalization, and cloud deployment.
content: Welcome to the Liquid Glass Template! This guide will walk you through setting up your development environment and customizing the template to fit your needs. Prerequisites Before you begin, make sure you have the following installed: - Node.js v18 or higher - pnpm (recommended) or npm - A code editor (VS Code recommended) We recommend using pnpm for faster, disk-efficient package management. Installation Clone the Repository First, clone the template repository to your local machine: Install Dependencies Install the project dependencies using your preferred package manager: Start the Development Server Run the development server to see your template in action: Your site should now be running at 🎉 Project Structure Here's an overview of the project's folder structure: - src/ - components/ - Hero.astro - About.astro - Pricing.astro - config/ - themes.ts - locales.ts - docs.ts - content/ - docs/ - en/ - ru/ - pages/ - index.astro - [theme].astro - styles/ - global.css - public/ - astro.config.mjs - package.json Choosing a Theme The template comes with 5 beautiful themes out of the box: | Theme | Description | |-------|-------------| | Liquid | Fluid animations, gradient backgrounds | | Glass | Glassmorphism effects, frosted panels | | Neo | Bold typography, strong contrast | | Luxury | Elegant gold accents, premium feel | | Minimal | Clean, focused, distraction-free | To switch themes, simply navigate to the theme switcher in the header or visit the theme demo pages directly. Next Steps Now that you have your development environment set up: 1. Explore the Themes — Learn about each theme's unique features 2. Internationalization Guide — Add support for more languages 3. Deployment Guide — Deploy to Cloudflare, Vercel, or Netlify Check out the FAQ or open an issue if you run into any problems.

title: Introduction
description: Welcome to the Liquid Glass documentation.
content: Introduction Liquid Glass is a premium Astro theme designed for startups and creators who want to stand out. It features a unique Glassmorphism design system built on top of Tailwind CSS. Why Liquid Glass? - Premium Design: Ready-to-use components with depth and blur effects. - Hybrid Performance: Statically generated content with server-side capabilities. - Developer Experience: Type-safe content collections and easy configuration. What's Included? The theme comes with over 20+ pre-built components, including: - 5 Hero variations - 5 Feature sections - 5 Pricing tables - Comprehensive Blog & Docs system

Translucency: Background colors use alpha channels (e.g., ). 3. Borders: Subtle 1px borders () define the edges. 4. Shadows: Soft, colored shadows create depth. title: Theming System
description: Understand the core architecture of our dynamic theming system, including CSS variables, theme registry, and variant rendering.
content: Our template features a highly flexible dynamic theming system built on top of Tailwind CSS and Astro's component architecture. Architecture Overview The theming system consists of three main layers: 1. Theme Registry: Definitions for each theme in . 2. CSS Custom Properties: Theme-aware variables defined in . 3. Dynamic Rendering: Section components that render variants based on the prop. Theme Registry Every theme must be registered in the file. This centralizes theme metadata and makes it available to the entire application. - src/ - config/ - themes.ts [modified] Each theme definition looks like this: CSS Variables We use standard CSS variables (custom properties) to handle theme-specific colors and effects. These variables are scoped to a data attribute on the or tag. Always use the prefix for theme variables to ensure consistency with our utility classes. Dynamic Component Loading Section components like act as wrappers. They dynamically import the correct theme variant based on the prop. This pattern allows for maximum flexibility. You can have completely different HTML structures for different themes while keeping a uniform API for the page templates. Creating a New Theme To add a new theme, follow these steps: 1. Add the theme definition to . 2. Define the new theme's CSS variables in . 3. (Optional) Create theme-specific components in , etc. 4. Add any new localized strings to the translation files.

title: Customization
description: How to customize styles, themes, and configuration.
content: Liquid Glass uses Tailwind CSS v4 for styling, which offers better performance and a streamlined configuration experience. Styling Overview Global styles and CSS variables are defined in . This file handles: - Base layer resets - Custom fonts (Inter & JetBrains Mono) - CSS variables for theming (HSL color values) - src/ - styles/ - global.css - tailwind.config.mjs Theming System The project uses a CSS variable-based theming system. Colors are defined as HSL values (without the ) function, allowing Tailwind's opacity modifier to work correctly. Components consume these variables via Tailwind utility classes or custom usage. To change the site's color scheme, update the HSL values in . You can define different values for light/dark mode using the selector if needed. Tailwind Configuration Tailwind v4 is configured in using the directive, but for backward compatibility or complex plugins, we also include a file. You can extend the theme, add plugins, or modify content paths in . Adding Custom Fonts 1. Place font files in or import from Google Fonts. 2. Define the font-face in . 3. Update the font family in . Component Customization Most UI components expose props for basic customization (like for Wrapper Components). For deeper changes, you should modify the component files directly in . title: Cloudflare Deployment
description: Deploy your Liquid Glass site to Cloudflare Pages.
content: This project is optimized for deployment on Cloudflare Pages. It includes the necessary adapter and configuration out of the box. Prerequisites - A Cloudflare account. - Node.js installed locally. - Wrangler CLI installed (). Deployment Methods You can deploy using GitHub integration (recommended) or via CLI. Option 1: GitHub Integration 1. Push your code to GitHub Ensure your project is in a GitHub repository. 2. Connect to Cloudflare Pages Go to the Cloudflare Dashboard > Workers & Pages > Create Application > Pages > Connect to Git. 3. Select Repository Choose your repository and branch. 4. Configure Build Settings Use the following settings: - Framework Preset: Astro - Build command: - Build output directory: Make sure to set the build command to npm run build # Note: Search indexing happens automatically during build via generate-search-index.mjs AND the post-build indexing script () required for search functionality. 5. Save and Deploy Option 2: Wrangler CLI You can also deploy directly from your terminal. 1. Login to Wrangler 2. Build and Deploy Run the deploy script defined in : This command executes: . Search Indexing The project uses Fuse.js for search. This requires a build-time step to generate the content index. The script in handles this automatically: If search isn't working on your deployed site, ensure that the indexing step ran successfully. Troubleshooting Deployment Fails Check the build logs. Common issues include TypeScript errors or missing dependencies. Search Not Working If search returns no results, check if the directory and / files were created during build. Ensure ran successfully.
